name: huffman
description: A static canonical Huffman codec for 8-bit symbols: an encoder that maps symbols to variable-length canonical codes and bit-packs them, and a decoder that recovers the symbols, wired as a self-checking loopback.
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Provenance (model and date) confirmed by the author; architecture, scope, and verification were directed and reviewed by the author.

spec.summary: Static canonical Huffman codec for 8-bit symbols. huffman_enc looks up a per-symbol {code, length} from a baked-in canonical ROM and feeds a bit-packer that concatenates codes MSB-first and emits output bytes, flushing the final partial byte on in_last; it streams with valid/ready. huffman_dec performs a bit-serial puff-style canonical decode using per-length codeword counts (cnt[L]) and a symbol-order ROM, streaming bytes in (valid/ready) and symbols out (valid). The huffman top wires the encoder's compressed byte stream straight into the decoder as a self-checking loopback, so decoded symbols equal the input symbols. The canonical code is static (256 8-bit symbols, max code length 13 bits, cap 15), built for a geometric frequency model freq[s] = round(1e6 * 0.98^s) and baked into combinational case ROMs generated by genhuff.py.
key_decisions: Static table-driven canonical Huffman (ROMs baked in by genhuff.py) rather than a dynamic tree builder, so the code table is fixed and fully synthesizable.

Encoder ROM is a combinational case on in_sym driving code and length; the low length bits are emitted MSB-first by a barrel-shift + accumulator bit-packer that flushes the final partial byte on in_last.

Decoder uses the compact puff-style canonical decode: a per-length codeword-count ROM (cnt) plus a canonical symbol-order ROM (dsym) and the canonical first-code recurrence, all as plain combinational case ROMs (no Verilog functions).

Frequency model is a geometric distribution freq[s] = round(1e6 * 0.98^s) giving shorter codes to smaller symbol values; max code length capped at 13 bits (cap 15), checked against the Kraft equality in the generator.
Top integrates encoder and decoder as a self-checking loopback example so a round-trip can be verified end to end.
Maps to LUTs and FFs only (ROMs, bit-packer, bit-serial decoder); no DSP and no BRAM.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench; follows the cited algorithm/standard and hardware architectures, not copied from any specific HDL source. The code table is generated by genhuff.py.

references: D. A. Huffman, 'A method for the construction of minimum-redundancy codes,' Proceedings of the IRE, vol. 40, no. 9, pp. 1098-1101, Sep. 1952.
DEFLATE Compressed Data Format Specification, RFC 1951, 1996 (canonical Huffman code construction and bit ordering).
M. Adler, puff.c (zlib contrib) -- the compact canonical Huffman decode (per-length count + symbol-order tables) that huffman_dec follows.
J. L. Nunez and S. Jones, 'Gbit/s lossless data compression hardware,' IEEE Trans. VLSI Systems, vol. 11, no. 3, pp. 499-510, 2003. (Huffman coder/bit-packer hardware)
